handoff_policy_design: P1 fixed cutoff provides the lowest control overhead and is the baseline.
P2 soft cutoff plus hard cap can admit only short units late in the turn.
P3 estimated-next-task admission explicitly budgets unit estimate plus close reserve plus safety margin.
P4 adapts reserve/margin from recent observations but risks overfitting and control overhead.
Compare policies on long-run useful_work/wall_clock, not only per-turn active seconds.
Track overshoot and unnecessary early handoff separately because both reduce policy quality.
Track estimate error for P3/P4 to determine whether prediction actually improves admission.
A complex policy that gains negligible utilization over P2 should be rejected.
Hard cap remains a safety invariant even under adaptive admission.
Late-turn units should be bounded/interruptible enough to preserve durable close.
Authority transfer and parallel successor optimization are downstream from establishing this safe admission envelope.
The final reusable contract should expose soft cutoff, hard cap, reserve, margin, and rollback rule explicitly.
